newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up across the board on Tuesday, with early-maturing contracts surging.
Traders said institutions borrowed heavily on the repo market to trade on the active domestic A share markets, pushing up the repo rates.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 16.2 percent from 11.20 percent on Monday.
Turnover rose to 11.15 million lots from 9.06 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

"Active trading on the Shanghai and Shenzhen A share markets attracted much liquidity from the repo market," one trader said. "But the rates are very high after today's surges and there is likely to be a technical correction tomorrow."
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down due to selling by big institutions, traders said. Volume of the nine-contract rose to 1.35 million lots from 1.07 million.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in 1999 fell to 113.59 yuan from 115 yuan.
The spot market has fallen in the past few months with liquidity flowing out into the more active A share markets.
